{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — EXHIBIT 10.4 (Hosting, Interface Licence and Support Services Agreement)

**To:** Deal team  
**From:** In-house counsel  
**Re:** Playbook review of EXHIBIT 10.4 (TrueLink / Client)  
**Privileged & Confidential — Attorney Work Product**

## Executive summary

We reviewed the Agreement against 18 playbook rules. Ten clauses are compliant and require no redline, several of them because the Agreement is silent where silence favours us (no exclusivity, no non-compete, no customer MFN, no audit right against us, no liquidated damages, no non-solicit). Term, renewal, termination for convenience and governing law all sit within our accepted range, and the minimum monthly commitment sits at our fallback.

Eight items require action. The most serious are the risk-allocation provisions: the indemnity in Section 12 is materially one-sided and the Agreement contains no third-party IP infringement indemnity from TrueLink at all, and the only liability cap protects TrueLink alone (12 months' compensation) while leaving our liability under the broad Client indemnity uncapped. We also need to fix the data licence in Section 8(d), which lets TrueLink independently exploit our Credit Data, and secure rights in the Support Services work product. Three expected clauses are absent entirely — post-termination transition and data return, a TrueLink performance warranty, and any insurance covenant. Finally, the assignment and licence provisions have no successor/M&A carve-out and no reasonableness standard on consent.

Our proposed redlines target the fallback positions except on indemnity, where we take the preferred position and therefore do not volunteer a super-cap.

## Findings

| Severity | Rule | Status | Section | Summary |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Deviation | § 12 Indemnity | Client indemnity broad; TrueLink indemnity limited to its own breach; no third-party IP indemnity anywhere. Fails fallback; approaches walk-away. |
| Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Deviation | § 8 Covenants and Warranties of Client | § 8(d) permits TrueLink to distribute, license, resell and exploit our Credit Data; no ownership or licence in Support Services work product. |
| High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Deviation | § 15 (per finding, cited at § 12 Indemnity) | Only a "financially responsible affiliate" carve-out, no successor/M&A carve-out, and no reasonableness standard on consent. |
| High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Deviation | § 2 License | Grant covers no affiliates (§ 8(c) limits access to Client personnel) and is not transferable to an M&A successor. |
| High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity binding Customer | Compliant | § 2 License | Non-exclusive licence; § 2(a) confirms we may acquire, develop or license competing systems. Preferred position met. |
| High | LD — Liquidated damages / penalties | Compliant | § 12 Indemnity (document-wide) | No liquidated damages, penalty or early-termination charge on Client. |
| High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete on Customer | Compliant | § 2 License | No restraint on our business or purchasing; the referenced Non-Competition Agreement constrains TrueLink. |
| High | T4C — Termination for convenience | Compliant | § 14 (per finding, cited at § 12 Indemnity) | Unconditional Client election, effective within roughly 60 days, no exit fee; meets fallback on all material terms. |
| Medium | LOL-CAP — Cap, mutuality and carve-outs | Deviation | § 12 Indemnity (cap at end of section) | One-way 12-month cap for TrueLink only, our liability uncapped (walk-away); no indemnity/confidentiality carve-outs; no consequential-damages exclusion. |
| Medium | TRANSITION — Transition assistance and data return | Missing | After § 14 (§ 13/§ 14 addressed) | No transition assistance, data return or deletion obligation; § 13 places the migration burden on Client. |
| Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty | Missing | After § 9 (§ 8 warranties run from Client) | Only a Year 2000 warranty from TrueLink; services owed on "reasonable commercial efforts" with no remedy. |
| Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Compliant | § 2 License (document-wide) | No TrueLink audit or verification right; § 5/§ 6 run in our favour. Better than fallback. |
| Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Compliant | §§ 26–27 (cited at § 12 Indemnity) | California law and exclusive California courts; sits at our fallback, no arbitration. |
| Medium | MFN — MFN burdening Customer | Compliant | § 5 Compensation | No MFN on Client; § 6 gives us a most-favoured-rate undertaking and a one-year price freeze. |
| Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum commitments | Compliant | § 5 Compensation | Monthly floor sits at fallback: term-limited, exitable under § 14, no shortfall or acceleration. Blank figures and cross-references to be conformed at signature. |
| Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation binding Customer | Compliant | § 8 Covenants and Warranties of Client | No non-solicit, no-hire or anti-inducement covenant anywhere. |
| Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and notice window | Compliant | § 13 (cited at § 12 Indemnity) | One-year renewals with 30-day mutual non-renewal notice; no uplift right. Meets fallback and most preferred elements. |
| Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | Missing | New § 31 (cited at § 12 Indemnity) | No insurance covenant at all for a vendor hosting the Web Site and processing our data (walk-away territory). |

## Walk-away items

The following findings engage walk-away territory under the playbook and should not be conceded without escalation:

1. **One-way liability cap (LOL-CAP, § 12).** TrueLink's liability is capped at 12 months' compensation while our liability under the broad Section 12a indemnity is unlimited. A Vendor-only cap with the Customer uncapped is walk-away territory; the cap must be made mutual.
2. **Absence of any TrueLink IP indemnity and materially one-sided indemnity (INDEMN, § 12).** No third-party infringement indemnity exists anywhere in the document, and TrueLink's indemnity is limited to its own breach. This fails the fallback and approaches walk-away.
3. **No insurance covenant (INSURANCE).** The absence of coverage for a vendor hosting the Web Site and processing our data is walk-away territory.
4. **No successor/M&A assignment carve-out (ASSIGN, § 15).** As drafted, the clause is walk-away territory on a merger or sale of substantially all assets.

## Next steps

1. **Issue the redline** on the five deviations and three missing clauses:
   - § 12: add a TrueLink defend-and-indemnify obligation for third-party IP claims, TrueLink's breach of law, TrueLink-caused unauthorized access to Client Content or Credit Data, and gross negligence or wilful misconduct, with notice, control and cooperation mechanics; narrow the Client indemnity to Client Content and Client's breach of law.
   - § 12 cap: make the 12-month cap mutual and apply it Agreement-wide, with indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence and wilful misconduct outside the cap.
   - § 8(d): limit TrueLink's Credit Data licence to providing the Hosting and Support Services; add a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense the Support Services work product.
   - § 2 / § 8(c): extend the licence to Client affiliates on written notice, permit transfer to an M&A successor, and conform the access covenant.
   - § 15: add a mutual successor carve-out on written notice (retaining the existing affiliate exception verbatim) and a not-unreasonably-withheld consent standard.
   - New clause after § 14: six months' transition assistance at then-current rates, data return in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, certified deletion thereafter.
   - New clause after § 9: 90-day Interface conformance warranty and 30-day services warranty with repair, replacement, re-performance or refund.
   - New § 31: E&O USD 1,000,000 and cyber/privacy USD 2,000,000.
2. **Complete the commercial blanks.** The minimum monthly amounts and Exhibits A and B remain blank, and the internal cross-references in § 6 ("minimum monthly fees listed in Section 4") and § 14 ("Subject to Section 4") should point to § 5. Business to confirm figures before signature.
3. **Preserve fallback positions in reserve.** On the cap we have not pressed the preferred greater-of USD 1,000,000 formulation, the mutual consequential-damages exclusion, or the data protection, fraud, IP and payment carve-outs; on insurance we have not asked for CGL, workers' compensation or certificate mechanics. These remain available as trade material.
4. **Note for the record, not for redline:** no vendor renewal reminder and no express CPI/3% uplift cap (RENEWAL); no injunctive-relief carve-out from the venue clause (GOVLAW); TrueLink's 30-day non-renewal notice (tracked under RENEWAL to avoid double-counting).
5. **Escalate** the four walk-away items to the deal principal if TrueLink resists, and confirm our position before any further concession."}
